newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to aid cellular sector with tariffs, credit.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to aid cellular sector with tariffs, credit.

text.p: Brazil announced Tuesday it would alter import tariffs and set up new credit lines to help local producers of cellular telephone equipment meet an expected "explosion" in demand.
It also introduced new rules for operators of specialized telecommunications services, including cable TV, data transfer, paging, trunking and satellite operations.

"Norms for all the services (in the telecommunications sector) have now been published," said Communications Minister Sergio Motta after he and President Fernando Henrique Cardoso signed decrees outlining the new rules.
Another document signed during a ceremony Tuesday authorizes the Industry and Commerce Ministry to begin a review of import tariffs that affect the cellular telephone industry.

Last week, Motta suggested eliminating existing tariffs of about 20 percent on components for cellular communications equipment and putting a tariff on completed cellular installations which currently enter Brazil tax-free.
A second stage of a plan to encourage local production of cellphones would involve low-interest credit lines offered to maunfacturers by the National Development Bank (BNDES).
"Brazilian companies, especially those requiring capital goods, need financing conditions similar to those of international suppliers," BNDES president Luiz Carlos Mendonca de Barros said.

Investment in cellular manufacturing in Brazil was expected to total between $6.0 and $8.0 billion over the next three years, Mendonca de Barros said, without specifying how much the bank might provide.
Fifteen consortia submitted bids to the Communications Ministry Monday for ten regional concessions to operate cellphone services.

The government's plan to allow private groups to offer cellular serivces on a so-called B Band system is expected to triple the number of Brazilian cellphone users to about six million by the end of next year.
The BNDES is also considering the possibility of privatizing A Band services currently provided by state-level subsidiaries of Telebras prior to the sale of the companies themselves.
